# A globally qualified radial operator escapes the relative-Maxwellian barrier

29 October2026. Actual normalized hard-sphere model, not Maxwell rates.
This is a positive operator/cost interface for a bounded SIGNED perturbation
query. It does not by itself provide a normalized continuous velocity sample.
The subsequent finite-observation positivity consumer is treated separately.

## 1. Representation and exact angular integration

Use beta=3/4, h=(f-M)/M^beta, and restrict to rotationally invariant sources
and solutions. This restriction is explicit, preserved by the model and
available to the ordinary isotropic deterministic/particle comparator.
Mass and energy matching imply int M^beta h=0 and int |w|^2 M^beta h=0.
The linearized gain kernel may therefore subtract a(V)+c(V)s^2, where V=|v|,
s=|w|. Its coefficient functions can depend on V, but its tested moment
space remains only the conserved radial mass/energy space.

Integrate the native kernel over the incoming direction BEFORE taking an
absolute value. With m=min(V,s), z=max(V,s), define

    F(x)=int_0^1 exp[x(1-u^2)/2]du
        =sum_(n>=0) x^n/(2n+1)!!,
    A(m)=4F(m^2)-m^2/3,
    k(V,s)=A(m)/z-z.                                   (R1)

At V=0 this is4/s-s. For m>0,
F(m^2)=sqrt(pi/2) exp(m^2/2)erf(m/sqrt2)/m.
The series shows A>=4 and A is increasing: its coefficients are4,1 and
4/(2n+1)!! for n>=2. Consequently k is increasing in m and decreasing
in z, an important enclosure fact.

To derive (R1), integrate4exp(v_perp^2/2)/|v-w| over uniform cosine.
Set r=|v-w|, D=V^2-s^2. Its integral is2/(Vs) times

    exp[(V^2+s^2)/4] int_(|V-s|)^(V+s)
             exp[-r^2/8-D^2/(8r^2)]dr.

The primitive is sqrt(pi/2) times the sum of
exp(-|D|/4)erf((r-|D|/r)/(2sqrt2)) and
exp(|D|/4)erf((r+|D|/r)/(2sqrt2)). The second term cancels at the two
endpoints; the first gives2sqrt(pi/2)exp(-|D|/4)erf(m/sqrt2).
Thus the averaged gain is4F(m^2)/z. The averaged loss is z+m^2/(3z).
This pays angular cancellation analytically, without a free conditional
average or an independent value for each direction.

## 2. Weighted row and actual finite certificate

Let rho_beta(s) be the normalized chi3 density of a Gaussian of variance
1/beta, and nu(V)=E_(W~M)|v-W|. The complete controlled row is

    J(V)=D(V)/nu(V) int rho_beta(s)|k(V,s)-a(V)-c(V)s^2|ds,
    D(V)=beta^(-3/2)exp[-(1-beta)V^2/2].                 (R2)

# A subcritical hard-sphere query and positive finite-observation output

29 October2026. Consumes the full-domain radial operator certificate, not its
finite preview. This is a restricted actual-hard-sphere operation with ideal
real/random primitives. Continuous full-velocity iid output and finite-bit
implementation are NOT claimed. Signed marks are only an intermediate;
Section7 gives an actually positive normalized observation consumer.

## 1. Acquired source class

M(v)=(2pi)^(-3/2)exp(-|v|^2/2), beta=3/4. Supply a radial nonnegative f0,
its exact density evaluator, mass1, mean0, energy3 and a warranted

    ||(f0-M)/M^beta||_infinity <=D=1/3200.

The ordinary comparator receives the same density, sampler and symmetry.
One explicit source is f_delta from POSITIVE_RESIDUAL_BARRIER.md, with
delta=2^-14. Its source bound is <=5delta M(0)^(1-beta)<5/16384<D.
All source parameters and sampling are explicit; no evolved density or
norm bound is an input. Other sources must actually qualify these premises.

## 2. Controlled mild equation

Let h=(f-M)/M^beta. Let Kc be the radial, mass/energy-controlled linear
kernel in RADIAL_OPERATOR_PROOF.md, and nu the known Maxwellian collision
frequency. The acquired coefficient is

    int |Kc(V,ds)| <=eta nu(V), eta=99/100.

Let Z_beta=int M^beta=(2pi)^(3/8)beta^(-3/2). Collision energy conservation
gives M^beta(p)M^beta(q)=M^beta(v)M^beta(w). Therefore the nonlinear term is

    N(h,h)(v)=int M^beta(w)|v-w| E_sigma
                    [h(p)h(q)-h(v)h(w)]dw.

Write nu_beta(v)=int M^beta(w)|v-w|dw. Gaussian scaling and radial convexity
give nu_beta/nu <=C_beta=Z_beta/sqrt(beta)<4. The last strict constant is a
plain rational/pi bound, not an unknown kinetic norm.

Use the mild equation with diagonal loss nu. For ||h||<=D, its nonlinear
term has norm at most2C_beta D^2 nu, and Lipschitz constant at most
4C_beta D nu. Hence the controlled map preserves the D-ball because

    eta+2C_beta D < eta+8D <1,

and is a contraction there because

    eta+4C_beta D < eta+16D=199/200.                    (U1)

These bounds hold on every time horizon, with the same constants, since
the diagonal exponential integral has mass at most1. They construct a
unique global bounded controlled mild solution; no future oracle or mixing
assumption is used.
